cases.sentence: Алеша махнул из дверей кучеру, и карета, привезшая доктора, подъехала к ___.
cases.explain: «выходным дверям» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: Ilusha The doctor came out of the room again, muffled in his fur coat and with his cap on his head. His face looked almost angry and disgusted, as though he were afraid of getting dirty. He cast a cursory glance round the passage, looking sternly at Alyosha and Kolya as he did so. Alyosha waved from the door to the coachman, and the carriage that had brought the doctor drove up. The captain darted out after the doctor, and, bowing apologetically, stopped him to get the last word. The poor fellow looked utterly crushed; there was a scared look in his eyes.

cases.sentence: Штабс-капитан стремительно выскочил вслед за доктором и, согнувшись, почти извиваясь пред ним, остановил его для ___.
cases.explain: «последнего слова» — after the preposition «для», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Ilusha The doctor came out of the room again, muffled in his fur coat and with his cap on his head. His face looked almost angry and disgusted, as though he were afraid of getting dirty. He cast a cursory glance round the passage, looking sternly at Alyosha and Kolya as he did so. Alyosha waved from the door to the coachman, and the carriage that had brought the doctor drove up. The captain darted out after the doctor, and, bowing apologetically, stopped him to get the last word. The poor fellow looked utterly crushed; there was a scared look in his eyes.

cases.sentence: — начал было он и не договорил, а лишь всплеснул руками в отчаянии, хотя все еще с последнею мольбой смотря на доктора, точно в ___ от теперешнего слова доктора мог измениться приговор над бедным мальчиком.
cases.explain: «самом деле» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Your Excellency, your Excellency … is it possible?” he began, but could not go on and clasped his hands in despair. Yet he still gazed imploringly at the doctor, as though a word from him might still change the poor boy’s fate.

cases.sentence: Я не Бог, — небрежным, хотя и привычно ___ ответил доктор.
cases.explain: «внушительным голосом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “I can’t help it, I am not God!” the doctor answered offhand, though with the customary impressiveness.

cases.sentence: — размахнул вдруг опять руками штабс-капитан, указывая в отчаянии на голые ___ сеней.
cases.explain: «бревенчатые стены» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Doctor, doctor! But you see!” The captain flung wide his hands again despairingly, indicating the bare wooden walls of the passage.

cases.sentence: — А, это уж не мое дело, — усмехнулся доктор, — я лишь сказал то, что могла сказать на-у-ка на ваш вопрос о ___, а остальное… к сожалению моему…
cases.explain: «последних средствах» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Well, that’s not my business,” grinned the doctor. “I have only told you the answer of medical science to your question as to possible treatment. As for the rest, to my regret—”

cases.sentence: — Не беспокойтесь, лекарь, моя собака вас не укусит, — громко отрезал Коля, заметив несколько ___ доктора на Перезвона, ставшего на пороге.
cases.explain: «беспокойный взгляд» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Don’t be afraid, apothecary, my dog won’t bite you,” Kolya rapped out loudly, noticing the doctor’s rather uneasy glance at Perezvon, who was standing in the doorway. There was a wrathful note in Kolya’s voice. He used the word apothecary instead of doctor on purpose, and, as he explained afterwards, used it “to insult him.”

cases.sentence: — Это ___, доктор, он шалун, не обращайте внимания, — нахмурившись и скороговоркой проговорил Алеша.
cases.explain: «здешний школьник» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “He is a schoolboy, doctor, he is a mischievous boy; take no notice of him,” said Alyosha, frowning and speaking quickly. “Kolya, hold your tongue!” he cried to Krassotkin. “Take no notice of him, doctor,” he repeated, rather impatiently.

cases.sentence: — Лекарь, есть только одно существо в ___, которое может приказывать Николаю Красоткину, это вот этот человек, — Коля указал на Алешу, — ему повинуюсь, прощайте!
cases.explain: «целом мире» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “There is only one man in the world who can command Nikolay Krassotkin—this is the man”; Kolya pointed to Alyosha. “I obey him, goodbye!”

cases.sentence: Я ведь знаю, что тебе ___ про меня сказал…
cases.explain: «новый доктор» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Ah, father! I know what the new doctor said to you about me. … I saw!” cried Ilusha, and again he hugged them both with all his strength, hiding his face on his father’s shoulder.
